newsitem.title: DUBAI: U.S. General Powell warns againt ousting Saddam.
newsitem.headline: U.S. General Powell warns againt ousting Saddam.

text.p: Retired Army General Colin Powell, who was the U.S. military's top officer during the 1991 Gulf war, has said taking stronger military action to oust Iraqi President Saddam Hussein would have serious consequences.

"Even if he (Saddam) was removed, that would mean Washington would be responsible for Iraq's future and destiny and finding an alternative leadership," he said in an interview with the Kuwaiti newspaper al-Rai al-Aam to be published on Saturday. An advance copy of the interview was made available to Reuters.

"It seems to me after studying the matter carefully when I was an official and years later that I truly don't see a second Thomas Jefferson in Iraq waiting for the chance to be the democratic leader to take charge of Iraq," Powell said.
"The problem facing the world and the allies is finding a successor to Saddam Hussein," he added.
U.S. cruise missiles hit Iraq this week in retaliation for Baghdad's weekend sweep into Kurdish-run northern Iraq.
Republican Richard Lugar, a senior member of the U.S. Senate Foreign Affairs Committee, has said President Bill Clinton had to go further in acting militarily against Saddam.
Powell sounded a note of caution against deeper American involvement in northern Iraq, where rival Kurdish factions are fighting each other.
"There is no reason now for American ground troop involvement. We do not have an obligation to get involved in the north," he was quoted by the newspaper as saying.
